DONATE BY CREDIT CARD
DONATE BY CHECK

GET A LAWN SIGN

Cupertino Together is a community organization committed to moving the city forward with a positive vision, steady leadership, and collaborative partnerships to create an enduring foundation for Cupertino’s present and future. We are starting with three strong candidates for Cupertino City Council.

OUR PRIORITIES
Seema, JR, and John will deliver real results for residents.
A real downtown finally built at Vallco
A fiscally stronger city
Simplified permits for homeowners and small businesses
Smart housing choices that protect our neighborhoods and our schools
Vibrant retail and restaurants
Trusted and stable governance
Meet the Council Candidates

JR Fruen

Jr is a sitting councilmember running for reelection. JR's family has called Cupertino home since before the city was incorporated, and he has spent a lifetime making sure it stays a place where every generation can put down roots. An attorney and current councilmember, he brings deep roots, legal expertise, and principled leadership to every decision — running for re-election on an unshakable conviction that we must leave things better than we found them.

Seema Sharma Lindskog

Seema is a current Cupertino Planning Commissioner. Her story spans multiple continents and cultures. Moving from India, she built a twenty-year career as a marketing executive, and spent the last decade delivering safer streets, thoughtful housing growth, and a more connected Cupertino. Now she's running for City Council to do even more — responsible housing for all life stages, innovative economic growth, and a safe, livable, vibrant city.

John Tang

John fled Vietnam as a child refugee and built the American dream through hard work, kindness, and a deep belief that strong communities lift everyone up. With 25 years navigating complex policy across government, business, and community, he is running for City Council to rebuild trust in city leadership and bring Vallco to life as a thriving hub for housing, jobs, and community.

Vote for all three...for the majority!
Five Great Reasons to Elect Seema, John, and JR
1. Finish Vallco to Finally Get a Downtown

10 years of litigation and delays have resulted in very little progress. Residents deserve a vibrant downtown.

Finally deliver the entertainment, dining, and retail that residents have waited a decade for.
Focus new housing in the Heart of the City near jobs, transit, and amenities.
Create the vibrant downtown destination that Cupertino deserves.
2. Restore Cupertino's Fiscal Strength

Losing Apple's sales tax cost Cupertino ~$30M/year. We must diversify our tax revenues, not rely on just one big company.

Attract midsized businesses to the city as Seema proposed to the City Council back in January 2025.
Complete Vallco to get $10 million in property taxes flowing each year plus sales and other taxes. 
Reduce reliance on expensive contractors by hiring full-time city staff instead.
3. Permits That Don't Punish You

Permits for home improvements, ADUs, and small business updates shouldn't require months of delay.

Streamline permits for simple home repairs and upgrades, as Seema proposed in Feb 2024.
Cut the permitting red tape driving small businesses out of Cupertino.
Continue to simplify and speed up home renovation, ADU, and duplex approval processes.
4. Housing for Young Families

CUSD lost 5,000 students since 2015, with 4,000 more projected. Fewer families means fewer schools, and aging city, and lower property values.

Prioritize starter homes that young families can actually afford and expand housing options for seniors and young professionals.
Allow more types of ADUs and duplexes–including for sale ones.
Focus denser housing on major streets near retail to protect our neighborhoods and support our small businesses.
5. Restore Good Governance

Cupertino needs stability after two damning Grand Jury reports, 9 City Managers in 8 years, and significant staff turnover.

Rebuild staff trust through open dialogue and data-driven decisions.
Strengthen protections from councilmanic interference and misuse of remote attendance.
Rebuild partnerships with regional agencies and leaders by leveraging John and JR’s networks.
Our priorities are an extension of our values.

Deliver a Vallco Downtown

Attract Young Families

Fix the City's Fiscal Mess

Revitalize Small Businesses

Cut Permitting Red Tape

By focusing on these key priorities, we will build a lasting future for Cupertino where our residents can thrive.
LEARN MORE ABOUT OUR PRIORITIES

Mail donations checks to Cupertino Together, 11807 Pine Brook Ct, Cupertino CA 95014. Make checks out separately for each candidate. We request 3 checks of equal amounts for each of the 3 candidates so that we can fully support our slate.

Residents
First

I am running for City Council

to put your quality of life,

safety, and future first.

JOIN THE MOVEMENT
As a lifelong resident, Cupertino parent, and community leader, I love this city.

From my roots as a proud Monta Vista graduate to my current role as Chair of the Cupertino Planning Commission, I have a lifelong care for our city. Now, I am running for Cupertino City Council for one reason alone: to ensure our government puts the community's needs first. 

Cupertino faces rising costs, neighborhoods disrupted by haphazard zoning, and retail loss. Cupertino deserves proactive policies that anticipate resident needs and greater accountability for every taxpayer dollar spent. City Council time must be dedicated to serving our community, not political agendas. I will deliver that focused leadership to Cupertino. I take no money from special interests, freeing me to serve you, the Cupertino community, first and foremost.

ISSUES
THE CUPERTINO COMMUNITY BACKS TRACY FOR COUNCIL

Current leaders, former elected official, and active residents trust Tracy to care about their city. Tracy has a track record of standing up for our community, and is determined to protect and uphold residents' quality of life, now and for generations to come.

SEE THE ENDORSEMENTS
DEDICATED TO CUPERTINO

As a proud Cupertino native, Planning Commission Chair, and active volunteer, Tracy is the Cupertino City Council candidate who will care for our city.

ABOUT SANTOSH
A neighbor first, a councilmember second.

Santosh Rao has worked in Cupertino starting 1998 and has called Cupertino home for over 11 years, raising his family and building deep roots here. He isn't running to climb a political ladder. He's running because he loves Cupertino and believes Cupertino deserves council members who put residents first and show up to work for residents long before and after election day.

A father of two, his children attended Stevens Creek Elementary, Faria Elementary, and are current students at Kennedy Middle and Monta Vista High. He chaired the Planning Commission in 2025 and continues to serve, sits on the CUSD Measure Z Bond Oversight Committee, and has served on Faria and Monta Vista school site councils, not as a stepping stone, but because the work matters.

"Cupertino deserves a council member who listens to residents, provides oversight on dais, and delivers results, not promises."

Santosh Rao

VOICES OF CUPERTINO · WHY THEY SUPPORT SANTOSH
Hear from your neighbors.

Community leaders and residents share in their own words why they believe in Santosh Rao for City Council, and why their vote is with him.

PRIORITIES · 06
What Santosh stands for

Six pillars guiding every vote, every meeting, every conversation. No vague promises. Concrete commitments with measurable progress.

01
NEIGHBORHOODS FIRST
Quality of Life

Vibrant events, beautiful parks, world-class public services, great roads, and a city where families want to stay for generations, not pass through on the way to somewhere else.

02
HONEST MATH
Fiscal Discipline

A budget that works for residents: long-horizon infrastructure investment, zero tolerance for wasteful spending, and full transparency so every resident can see where the money goes.

03
RESPECT WHAT WORKS
Sensible Development

Affordable housing AND neighborhood character: context-appropriate density, protecting single-family corridors while encouraging thoughtful housing on main corridors. Both. Not one or the other.

04
SMALL BUSINESS FRIENDLY
Pro-Business

Reduce bottlenecks to working with Cupertino, attract diverse retail and dining, and treat small business owners as partners, not paperwork problems.

05
PARTNER WITH CUSD & FUHSD
Education & Schools

The City and the Districts should be in lockstep: safe crosswalks, well-maintained fields, and reasonable city resources backing the educators who make this community shine.

06
CALM, PRESENT, ACCOUNTABLE
Public Safety

Traffic enforcement, law enforcement, engaging the community, modern emergency response, and smart technology for road and traffic management, backed by data the public can see.

TRACK RECORD · EXPERIENCED LEADERSHIP
Showing up long before election day.

Six active civic roles, from Planning Commission Chair to school site councils. The work started well before this campaign, and it won't stop after November.

Ongoing
CHAIR
CITY OF CUPERTINO
Cupertino Planning Commission

Chaired all land-use, development, and long-range planning decisions for the city in 2025 and continues to serve as Planning Commissioner. Driving a more responsive, resident-centered process for permits and community projects.

Ongoing

CUPERTINO UNION SCHOOL DISTRICT
Measure Z Bond Oversight Committee

Independent oversight of bond expenditures. Ensuring every dollar reaches the classroom, with full public transparency on project status and spending.

2023–25

School Site Councils

Active member at both schools his children attend, shaping budgets, educational priorities, and student support programs at the community level. Also served on Stevens Creek Elementary Site Council.

2022–25
ADVOCATE
FARIA ELEMENTARY & MONTA VISTA HIGH
Safe Routes to School

Parent representative for Safe Routes to School at both Faria Elementary and Monta Vista High, advocating for funded crosswalk and traffic-calming improvements on school commute corridors.

captures.text:
Join Our Campaign
DONATE BY CREDIT CARD
DONATE BY CHECK
VOLUNTEER
GET A LAWN SIGN

Cupertino Together is a community organization committed to moving the city forward with a positive vision, steady leadership, and collaborative partnerships to create an enduring foundation for Cupertino’s present and future. We are starting with three strong candidates for Cupertino City Council.

OUR PRIORITIES
Seema, JR, and John will deliver real results for residents.
A real downtown finally built at Vallco
A fiscally stronger city
Simplified permits for homeowners and small businesses
Smart housing choices that protect our neighborhoods and our schools
Vibrant retail and restaurants
Trusted and stable governance
Meet the Council Candidates

JR Fruen

Jr is a sitting councilmember running for reelection. JR's family has called Cupertino home since before the city was incorporated, and he has spent a lifetime making sure it stays a place where every generation can put down roots. An attorney and current councilmember, he brings deep roots, legal expertise, and principled leadership to every decision — running for re-election on an unshakable conviction that we must leave things better than we found them.

Seema Sharma Lindskog

Seema is a current Cupertino Planning Commissioner. Her story spans multiple continents and cultures. Moving from India, she built a twenty-year career as a marketing executive, and spent the last decade delivering safer streets, thoughtful housing growth, and a more connected Cupertino. Now she's running for City Council to do even more — responsible housing for all life stages, innovative economic growth, and a safe, livable, vibrant city.

John Tang

John fled Vietnam as a child refugee and built the American dream through hard work, kindness, and a deep belief that strong communities lift everyone up. With 25 years navigating complex policy across government, business, and community, he is running for City Council to rebuild trust in city leadership and bring Vallco to life as a thriving hub for housing, jobs, and community.

Vote for all three...for the majority!
Five Great Reasons to Elect Seema, John, and JR
1. Finish Vallco to Finally Get a Downtown

10 years of litigation and delays have resulted in very little progress. Residents deserve a vibrant downtown.

Finally deliver the entertainment, dining, and retail that residents have waited a decade for.
Focus new housing in the Heart of the City near jobs, transit, and amenities.
Create the vibrant downtown destination that Cupertino deserves.
2. Restore Cupertino's Fiscal Strength

Losing Apple's sales tax cost Cupertino ~$30M/year. We must diversify our tax revenues, not rely on just one big company.

Attract midsized businesses to the city as Seema proposed to the City Council back in January 2025.
Complete Vallco to get $10 million in property taxes flowing each year plus sales and other taxes. 
Reduce reliance on expensive contractors by hiring full-time city staff instead.
3. Permits That Don't Punish You

Permits for home improvements, ADUs, and small business updates shouldn't require months of delay.

Streamline permits for simple home repairs and upgrades, as Seema proposed in Feb 2024.
Cut the permitting red tape driving small businesses out of Cupertino.
Continue to simplify and speed up home renovation, ADU, and duplex approval processes.
4. Housing for Young Families

CUSD lost 5,000 students since 2015, with 4,000 more projected. Fewer families means fewer schools, and aging city, and lower property values.

Prioritize starter homes that young families can actually afford and expand housing options for seniors and young professionals.
Allow more types of ADUs and duplexes–including for sale ones.
Focus denser housing on major streets near retail to protect our neighborhoods and support our small businesses.
5. Restore Good Governance

Cupertino needs stability after two damning Grand Jury reports, 9 City Managers in 8 years, and significant staff turnover.

Rebuild staff trust through open dialogue and data-driven decisions.
Strengthen protections from councilmanic interference and misuse of remote attendance.
Rebuild partnerships with regional agencies and leaders by leveraging John and JR’s networks.
Our priorities are an extension of our values.

Deliver a Vallco Downtown

Attract Young Families

Fix the City's Fiscal Mess

Revitalize Small Businesses

Cut Permitting Red Tape

By focusing on these key priorities, we will build a lasting future for Cupertino where our residents can thrive.
LEARN MORE ABOUT OUR PRIORITIES
Donate by Check

Mail donations checks to Cupertino Together, 11807 Pine Brook Ct, Cupertino CA 95014. Make checks out separately for each candidate. We request 3 checks of equal amounts for each of the 3 candidates so that we can fully support our slate. 

Seema Lindskog for Cupertino City Council 2026
John Tang for Cupertino City Council 2026
J.R. Fruen for Cupertino City Council 2026

FPPC Requirement: All checks must include a note listing your address, employer and occupation. If not employed, please indicate "Not Employed" or "Retired".
